描述_EN: however, patterned silk was a luxiorus commodity and every spare inch would have been utilised, as can be seen in the gore where two small pieces been stitched together with no apparent consideration to the motifs. however, the pattern might have been misunderstood by the tailor as it is utilised 'upside-down' as well as in correct reading orientation. the pattern of the silk consist of a palmette or lotus design with the stylized chinese character shou, meaning 'longevity'. this might suggest that at least the tailoring was done in a context where the reading of chinese characters was irrelevant. this fragment is part of a group of chinese silks in the v&a collection, broadly dated between the late thirteenth century and the mid-fifteenth century, and supposedly came from egypt. the one shown here, in blue damask, appears to be a section of a garment showing presumably a side seam with a gore insertion.
描述_ZN: 然而，有图案的丝绸是一种奢侈的商品，每一个空闲的地方都会被利用，就像在这个伤口上可以看到的那样，两块小的丝绸被缝在一起，没有明显考虑到图案。 然而，这个图案可能被裁缝误解了，因为它是被 "颠倒 "使用的，而不是在正确的阅读方向。 丝绸的图案包括一个棕榈或莲花的设计，上面有 "寿 "字，意思是长寿。 这可能表明，至少裁缝是在与汉字的阅读无关的情况下完成的。 这块碎片是V&A收藏的一组中国丝绸的一部分，时间大致在13世纪末和15世纪中，据说来自埃及。 这里显示的是蓝色锦缎，似乎是一件衣服的一部分，大概显示的是一个侧缝，有一个孔的插入。
